name: AJJ Muscoth Alwa
description: The traditional AJJ Muscoth Halwa (famous from Mudalur, Tamil Nadu) is made with just four primary ingredients: refined flour (maida or wheat milk), thick coconut milk, sugar (or jaggery), and cashew nuts. A key feature of this Sri Lankan-inspired halwa is that it uses no added oil or ghee—its glossy texture comes entirely from the natural oils extracted from the coconut milk.

name: Kadalai Mittai (Peanut Candy)
description:
Kadalai mittai (also known as peanut chikki or groundnut candy) is a traditional Indian sweet. It is made with just a few simple, natural ingredients:
Peanuts (Groundnuts): The main base of the candy.

Jaggery (Vellam): The unrefined sugar used to bind and sweeten the peanuts.

Water: Used to melt the jaggery into a thick syrup.

Cardamom Powder: Adds a warm, sweet flavor (optional but common).

Ghee: Used in small amounts for greasing hands when rolling the candy into balls.

A Pinch of Salt: Enhances the sweetness.

name: Athirasam
description:
Raw Rice (Pacharisi): 1 cup (preferably soaked and ground fresh at home while still slightly moist).
Jaggery (Paagu Vellam): ¾ cup to 1 cup, powdered or grated (dark palm or cane jaggery gives the best color and deep flavor).
Water: ¼ to ½ cup (used to melt the jaggery)

name: Jalebi
description: Jalebi needs a fermented or instant batter piped into hot oil and soaked in sugar syrup. The main components are all-purpose flour, yogurt or lemon juice for sourness, baking soda or yeast for rise, and sugar, saffron, and cardamom for the sweet syrup. You can check out a detailed walkthrough on the Indian Healthy Recipes Jalebi Guide for exact proportions

name: Sillu Karupatti
description: Sillu Karupatti (a traditional South Indian palm jaggery) is a natural unrefined sweetener often enriched with spices. The exact ingredients vary by brand, but they generally consist of pure palm sap (Neera) and a blend of traditional medicinal herbs.

name: Seeni Seevu
description: The ultimate sweet-and-savory paradox. These crisp, fried ribbon strips are dusted or coated in a delicate sugar (seeni) glaze, creating a unique flavor profile where a hint of salt perfectly complements a gentle sweetness.

name: Seeval
description:
Seeval (or Ribbon Pakoda) is a crunchy South Indian snack. Its core ingredients are:
Flours: Gram flour (besan) and rice flour.

Fats: Melted butter, ghee, or hot oil.

Spices: Chili powder, asafoetida (hing), and salt.

Frying Medium: Groundnut or vegetable oil

name: Sevu (Sathur)
description: Sevu (or Sev) is a famous, crispy Indian snack made from deep-fried chickpea flour (besan) dough. It is shaped into thin, noodle-like strands and is widely enjoyed across South Asia. It can be eaten on its own, used as a crunchy topping for dishes like chaat, or mixed into snacks like Bombay Mix.

name: Big Mixture
description: A grand celebration of traditional South Indian flavors. This premium, crispy medley combines thick, crunchy seevu, golden fried savory elements, nuts, and aromatic curry leaves tossed in a perfectly balanced spice blend.

name: Small Mixture
description: The perfect everyday tea-time companion. This finely blended savory mix features delicate, bite-sized components, crispy sev, and subtle spices that deliver a satisfying crunch without overwhelming the palate.

name: Milagu (Black Pepper) Seevu
description: A fiery, nostalgic treat crafted for spice lovers. Made with high-quality gram flour and generously infused with the bold, earthy heat of freshly crushed black pepper (milagu), these ribbon-shaped strips deliver a deep, warming kick.

name: Masala Kadalai
description: Bold, crunchy, and irresistibly nutty. Premium whole peanuts are coated in a spiced, fiery chickpea flour batter and fried to a deep golden crisp, making every bite an explosion of garlic, chili, and nutty flavor.

name: Ragi Murukku
description: The perfect blend of heritage nutrition and modern snacking. Crafted from wholesome finger millet (ragi) flour and traditional spices, this deep-crimson, spiral murukku offers an ultra-shattery crispness with a rich, earthy flavor.

name: Oma Podi
description: Delicately thin, golden savory strands infused with the unmistakable, soothing aroma of carom seeds (omam). Light on the stomach and melt-in-your-mouth crispy, it is as comforting as it is delicious.

name: Poondu Murukku (Small Murukku)
description: Poondu Murukku (Garlic-Small Murukku) is a crunchy, bite-sized South Indian savoury snack made primarily from a dough of rice flour and gram flour (besan or urad dal). It gets its distinct, bold taste and irresistible aroma from a generous infusion of freshly blended garlic paste and spicy red chillies. Shaped using a traditional kitchen press into mini, compact spirals or spiked logs, it is deep-fried in hot oil until it reaches a flawless golden, light, and shattered-crisp texture.

name: Banana Chips
description: Banana Chips are a premium, all-natural South Indian snack made from thinly sliced, unripe green bananas (typically the Nendran variety) deep-fried in pure, cold-pressed coconut oil.
